name: set_char_opts
title: Format a character vector in a tibble

origin.description: Attach min_chars and shorten to an existing vector and leave its data in place.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: The vector that receives the pillar attribute. Its values are not changed.

arguments.name: min_chars
arguments.text: Minimum width stored on the pillar attribute. NULL omits it.

arguments.name: shorten
arguments.text: Omitted or NULL stores nothing. Otherwise one of "back", "front", "mid", or "abbreviate". The match is exact.

origin.details: The attribute is the same one char() stores, and format of it is the same type label. This function does not add the pillar_char class, so a plain character vector stays a character vector and its abbreviation stays chr. char() calls this and then marks the result.
origin.value: x, with a pillar attribute and the same data.
origin.example:
x <- set_char_opts(c("a", "bb"), min_chars = 5, shorten = "mid")
x
format(attr(x, "pillar"))
vctrs::vec_ptype_abbr(x)
y <- set_char_opts(c("a", NA), shorten = "back")
y
format(attr(y, "pillar"))
z <- set_char_opts("hello", shorten = "abbreviate")
format(attr(z, "pillar"))

translation.description: The same attribute on the existing data. The result stays unmarked unless x was already a pillar_char.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A string, None, a list of strings, or an existing PillarChar. The values are copied and kept.

arguments.name: min_chars
arguments.text: Stored and printed inside the type label. None omits it.

arguments.name: shorten
arguments.text: None, or one of "back", "front", "mid", or "abbreviate". A prefix is rejected.

translation.details: format_pillar_char_attr is the type label. A plain character result has abbreviation chr. Passing the result of char() keeps the pillar_char mark and replaces the options.
translation.value: A PillarChar. data is the original data. marked is false for a plain vector.
translation.example:
from pillar.char import format_pillar_char_attr, set_char_opts, vec_ptype_abbr

x = set_char_opts(["a", "bb"], min_chars=5, shorten="mid")
print(x.data)
print(format_pillar_char_attr(x.pillar))
print(vec_ptype_abbr(x))
y = set_char_opts(["a", None], shorten="back")
print(y.data)
print(format_pillar_char_attr(y.pillar))
z = set_char_opts("hello", shorten="abbreviate")
print(format_pillar_char_attr(z.pillar))
